title: Chicken thigh, fried, coated, skinless, coating eaten, from raw

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken thigh that has been deep‑fried in a breaded coating. Made from raw product code 846, it retains a high protein level while the coating adds a crunchy texture and extra flavor. This dish is common in main courses, fast‑food menus, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken thighs contain more fat than breast meat, making them juicier when fried.
Deep‑frying at 175‑190 °C creates a golden crust while keeping the interior moist.
The coating can be made from wheat flour, breadcrumbs, spices, and sometimes cornmeal crumbs.
Often served with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, or garlic aioli.
In some cuisines (e.g., South American) the thighs are marinated in lime and paprika before breading.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken thigh provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Supplies iron, zinc, and phosphorus, essential for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Fatty acids
items.content: The fat retained after frying includes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated acids that, in moderation, are heart‑healthy.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat promotes a lasting feeling of fullness.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying increases calories; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Using oils high in saturated fat can raise cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Food allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to wheat in the breading.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen; avoid over‑cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Breaded chicken thighs are convenient as a hot snack, added to salads, sandwiches, or served with sides such as potatoes, rice, or vegetables. Pair with a variety of dipping sauces to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consumption.
